## Results

The intervention improved scores, t(28) = 2.20, p = .004, and a second test gave t(40) = 2.10, p = .042.
Participants rated satisfaction (M = 3.48, SD = 1.20, n = 15). A second group scored M = 3.47, n = 15.
Of the sample, 35.7% (n = 28) reported symptoms, and 33.3% (n = 28) did not.
Accuracy was 85.2% ± 60.1% across folds, and recall 0.91 ± 0.40.
Error fell from 12.0% to 9.0%, a 25% relative reduction, and latency from 200 ms to 150 ms, a 40% reduction.
Throughput rose from 10 to 35, a 3.5-fold increase, and loss from 0.50 to 0.40, a 0.1 point drop.
Our method outperforms the baseline (81.2 ± 2.1 vs 80.4 ± 1.9).
On a 7-point scale the mean was 4.1 ± 3.5.
